questions.question: A toy boat is pulled northwards with a force of 12 N by a string, while the water current pushes it southwards with a force of 4 N, and the wind blows it southwards with a force of 3 N. What is the resultant force on the boat?
options: 19 N Northwards
5 N Northwards
5 N Southwards
9 N Northwards

questions.question: A sledge is pulled to the right with a force of 45 N by a child, while a friction force of 30 N acts to the left. In which direction will the resultant force act, and why?
options: To the right, because the pulling force is greater than the friction force.
To the left, because friction always overcomes pulling forces.
It will not act in any direction because the forces are balanced.
To the right, because the sledge is already moving to the right.

questions.question: Four identical toy cars (A, B, C, and D) are pushed along a frictionless track with different resultant forces. Car A has a resultant force of 2 N, Car B has 5 N, Car C has 1.5 N, and Car D has 4 N. Which car's speed will change most rapidly?
options: Car C
Car A
Car D
Car B

questions.question: A raised heavy hammer has gravitational potential energy store. In physics terms, what does having this energy store fundamentally mean for the hammer before it is released?
options: It contains a physical fluid called energy that will spill out upon impact.
It possesses properties that allow it to interact with and cause changes to a nail when dropped.
It is guaranteed to stay suspended indefinitely without any external support.
It has lost its mass and became pure force ready to do work.

questions.question: A student slides a heavy wooden block across a smooth ice rink and then across a concrete playground with the same initial push. Why does the block stop much sooner on the concrete?
options: Concrete exerts a larger gravitational pull on the block than ice does.
The concrete surface provides a much larger friction force that opposes and slows down the block's movement.
The block's mass decreases as it slides on concrete, reducing its forward momentum.
Air resistance is significantly higher over concrete surfaces than over ice.

questions.question: At a microscopic level, even highly polished metal sheets have tiny bumps and ridges. How does this microscopic structure explain the origin of friction when two such sheets slide over each other?
options: The microscopic ridges interlock and collide, resisting the relative movement between the surfaces.
The ridges create pocket vacuums that suck the two sheets together.
The air trapped between the ridges acts as a strong glue.
The rough ridges generate electrostatic repulsion that pushes the plates apart.

questions.question: A bicycle chain is squeaking and stiff. After applying a thin layer of oil, the pedals turn much more easily. Which statement best explains how the oil achieved this effect?
options: The oil reacts chemically with the metal to make the chain lighter.
The oil fills the microscopic gaps and separates the rough surfaces, reducing the friction between them.
The oil increases the contact area to increase the grip between the chain and the gears.
The oil acts as an adhesive that binds the chain links tightly together.

questions.question: A student notices that when a newton meter is hanging empty, the pointer rests at the 0.5 N mark instead of 0 N. If they use this meter to measure a 4.0 N weight without adjusting it, what will the scale read, and how should they fix this?
options: It will read 3.5 N; they should subtract 0.5 N from all readings.
It will read 4.5 N; they should adjust the zero calibration screw to align the pointer with 0 N before measuring.
It will read 4.5 N; they must buy a new meter as this one is permanently damaged.
It will read 4.0 N; the error automatically corrects itself when a load is added.

questions.question: A student wants to measure a force that they estimate to be around 2.4 N. They have three newton meters available: Meter X (range 0–1 N, divisions of 0.1 N), Meter Y (range 0–5 N, divisions of 0.1 N), and Meter Z (range 0–100 N, divisions of 5 N). Which meter is the most appropriate choice?
options: Meter X, because it has the smallest divisions and will be highly precise.
Meter Z, because its large scale ensures it will not break under any circumstances.
Meter Y, because its scale accommodates the force and offers detailed divisions for an accurate reading.
Either Meter Y or Meter Z, as the total range of the meter does not affect readability.

questions.question: A group of students tests how much force is needed to slide a wooden block across different floor coverings: carpet, vinyl, wood, and concrete. What type of chart should they use to display their results, and why?
options: A line graph, because both the floor covering and the force are continuous variables.
A bar chart, because the independent variable (type of floor covering) is categoric.
A scatter graph, because there are multiple trials for each floor type.
A pie chart, because they need to show the proportion of total force used on each floor.

questions.question: To investigate how the surface area of a parachute affects its fall time, students drop parachutes of different sizes. To ensure this is a fair test, what must they do regarding the variables?
options: Change both the surface area and the mass of the parachutes at the same time.
Change only the surface area of the parachute, keeping all other variables like mass and drop height the same.
Keep the surface area constant and change the material of each parachute.
Change the drop height for each different parachute size.

questions.question: A student measures the friction force of a shoe on wood three times, getting results of 4.2 N, 4.1 N, and 8.9 N. What is the value of repeating this measurement, and how should they handle the 8.9 N result?
options: It confirms all results are reliable, so they should calculate the mean of all three values.
It helps identify the 8.9 N reading as an anomaly, which should be investigated and excluded before calculating the mean.
It shows that the shoe grew heavier during the third test, so the third reading is the most accurate.
It proves that the equipment is broken, so they should discard all results and start a different experiment.

questions.question: A magnet is held 2 cm above a steel paperclip, causing the paperclip to jump up and stick to the magnet. Which statement correctly describes the magnetic force during this event?
options: It is a contact force because the paperclip eventually touches the magnet.
It is a non-contact force because it pulled the paperclip upwards before they were touching.
It is only a force once the physical contact is established.
It is a contact force that acts through the air molecules pushing the paperclip.

questions.question: A skydiver is falling through the air before opening their parachute. What is the nature of the drag force acting on the skydiver?
options: It is a non-contact force of gravity pulling the skydiver upwards.
It is a contact force caused by the skydiver's body colliding with and pushing through air particles.
It is an electromagnetic force field generated by the rapid motion.
It is a constant downward force that increases their speed of descent.

questions.question: In a force diagram of a rising hot air balloon, the upward thrust arrow is drawn 6 cm long, while the downward gravity arrow is drawn 4 cm long. What do these lengths tell us about the forces?
options: The downward force of gravity is larger because it is more concentrated.
The upward thrust force is larger than the downward gravity force.
Both forces are equal because they are acting on the same balloon.
The balloon is moving horizontally because the arrows have different lengths.

questions.question: A book rests quietly on a wooden table. How should the upward support force acting on the book be labeled according to scientific standards?
options: The force acting on the table by the book.
The force acting on the book by gravity.
The force acting on the book by the table.
The force acting on the table by the floor.

questions.question: Two grocery trolleys are in a supermarket. Trolley X is empty, while Trolley Y is fully loaded with heavy canned goods. Why is Trolley Y much harder to suddenly turn around a corner than Trolley X?
options: Trolley Y has a greater mass, so it requires a greater force to change its direction of motion.
Trolley Y experiences less friction from the floor, making it slide out of control.
Trolley X has more chemical energy, which assists the shopper in steering it.
Trolley Y is subject to a stronger magnetic field from the floor.

questions.question: A tennis ball is flying through the air. In which of the following situations is a force NOT being applied to the ball?
options: The ball hits the racket, causing it to compress and change shape.
The ball strikes the court surface and bounces upward, changing its direction.
The ball continues to fly in a straight line at a completely constant speed in deep, empty space.
The ball slows down as it travels through the air due to air resistance.

questions.question: A cyclist travels along a straight, flat road. The forward force from their pedaling is exactly 40 N, and the backward drag force is exactly 40 N. Which of the following describes the cyclist's motion?
options: The cyclist will gradually slow down and eventually come to a stop.
The cyclist will continue moving forward at a constant speed because there is no resultant force.
The cyclist will instantly stop moving because the forces cancel out.
The cyclist will accelerate forward because the pedaling force was applied first.

questions.question: An archer pulls back a bowstring, bending the bow. In terms of energy and forces, what is happening during this process?
options: The force applied by the archer's hands transfers energy into the elastic store of the bow by changing its shape.
Energy is destroyed by the force of friction as the string moves backward.
The bow creates new energy because of the tension force within its material.
No energy is transferred because the bow is not yet moving through the air.

questions.question: A book is resting on a table. The earth pulls down on the book with a force of 5 N, and the table pushes up on the book with a force of 5 N. Which statement correctly describes this scenario?
options: The forces are balanced because they are equal in size and act in opposite directions.
The forces are unbalanced because they act on different objects.
The forces are balanced because they are equal in size and act in the same direction.
The forces are unbalanced because gravity is stronger than the support force of the table.

questions.question: A toy car has a forward force of 10 N pushing it to the right and a friction force of 4 N pulling it to the left. What is the resultant force acting on the car?
options: 14 N to the right
6 N to the right
6 N to the left
14 N to the left

questions.question: An ice hockey puck is sliding across a perfectly smooth, frictionless ice rink at a constant speed of 5 meters per second. What can we conclude about the forces acting on the puck in the direction of its motion?
options: There is a small forward force keeping it in motion.
The forward force must be slightly larger than the backward force.
The forces in the direction of motion are balanced, resulting in zero net force.
The backward force of friction is gradually slowing it down.

questions.question: During a tug-of-war, Team A pulls to the left with a force of 450 N, while Team B pulls to the right with a force of 500 N. In which direction does the resultant force act?
options: To the left, because Team A has less friction.
To the right, because Team B exerts the larger force.
It does not act in any direction because the forces cancel out.
Downwards, due to the combined mass of both teams.

questions.question: Two identical shopping carts are pushed with different forces. Cart X is pushed with a resultant force of 10 N, while Cart Y is pushed with a resultant force of 30 N. What will be the difference in their motion?
options: Cart X will change its speed faster than Cart Y.
Cart Y will change its speed faster than Cart X.
Both carts will change their speed at the exact same rate.
Cart Y will immediately stop, while Cart X will continue to accelerate.

questions.question: A student winds up a toy car by compressing its internal spring and then places it on the floor. Which energy store increases as the spring is compressed?
options: Gravitational store
Thermal store
Kinetic store
Elastic store

questions.question: Why is it much harder to slide a heavy wooden crate across a rough concrete floor than across a smooth polished wooden floor?
options: The concrete floor creates a larger contact area with the crate.
Friction between the crate and the rough concrete is greater, slowing down or preventing movement.
The concrete floor exerts a stronger magnetic pull on the crate.
There is no friction acting on the polished wooden floor.

questions.question: When bicycle chains become dry, they are hard to pedal and squeak. Adding chain oil makes pedaling much smoother. How does the oil achieve this effect?
options: The oil acts as a lubricant that is added between the moving surfaces to reduce friction.
The oil increases the grip between the metal links to prevent slipping.
The oil increases the mass of the chain, giving it more kinetic energy.
The oil chemically melts away the rough parts of the metal permanently.

questions.question: Before starting an experiment to measure the weight of different wooden blocks, a student notices that the pointer on their spring balance (newton meter) points to 0.5 N when nothing is hanging from it. What must the student do?
options: Subtract 0.5 N from only the first measurement they record.
Adjust the newton meter to read zero when no force is applied.
Ignore the error because it will not affect the final conclusions.
Multiply all subsequent readings by 0.5 to correct the scale.

questions.question: A student wants to measure a force that they estimate to be around 8.5 N. They have four newton meters available with different scales. Which meter is the most appropriate to choose?
options: A 0 to 1 N meter with 0.1 N divisions.
A 0 to 5 N meter with 0.5 N divisions.
A 0 to 10 N meter with 0.1 N divisions.
A 0 to 100 N meter with 10 N divisions.

questions.question: A student tests how different types of surfaces (carpet, wood, tile, bubble wrap) affect the distance a toy car travels. What type of chart should they use to display their results, and why?
options: A line graph, because both variables are continuous.
A bar chart, because the independent variable (surface type) is categoric.
A scatter graph, because they are looking for a numerical correlation.
A pie chart, because the total distance must equal 100%.

questions.question: After completing an investigation on friction, a student writes: 'We found that rougher surfaces cause more friction. This is because the wooden block required a force of 4.2 N to slide on sandpaper, but only 1.5 N on polished wood.' Why is this a good conclusion?
options: It states what was found out and also explains how the data supports it.
It lists all the raw data collected without making any claims.
It describes the step-by-step method used during the experiment.
It suggests improvements that could be made to the experimental setup.

questions.question: In an experiment investigating how the mass of a toy car affects the distance it rolls down a ramp, which of the following describes how a fair test is maintained?
options: The height of the ramp, the surface of the ramp, and the release method are kept the same for every measurement.
A different ramp height is used for each mass to keep the speed constant.
The mass of the car is kept constant while changing the surface of the ramp.
Multiple students release the car at different times using different techniques.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a force with its classification as a contact force?
options: Friction, because it only acts when two surfaces are touching.
Gravity, because it pulls objects down when they touch the ground.
Magnetism, because magnets must touch to attract or repel.
Static electricity, because hair must touch a balloon to be attracted.

questions.question: A piece of paper is attracted upwards towards a statically charged plastic ruler without the ruler actually touching the paper. Which statement best explains this?
options: Static electricity is a contact force that only works through air currents.
The paper is experiencing a non-contact force, which can act without the objects touching.
The ruler is creating a temporary gravitational field that pulls the paper.
A contact force is acting because the air molecules are pushing the paper.

questions.question: A skydiver is falling through the air. As their speed increases, they feel a growing upward force pushing against their movement. What is the correct term and classification for this force?
options: Drag, which is a non-contact force that acts through a vacuum.
Friction, which is a non-contact force that only acts on solid metals.
Drag, which is a contact force that pushes against objects moving through liquids or gases.
Gravity, which is a contact force pushing upwards against the skydiver.

questions.question: In a physics diagram, two forces acting on a box are represented by arrows. Arrow A is twice as long as Arrow B. What does this difference in length represent?
options: Arrow A represents a force that acts over a longer distance than Arrow B.
Arrow A represents a force of greater size (magnitude) than Arrow B.
Arrow A represents a force that acts for a longer duration than Arrow B.
Arrow A represents a contact force, while Arrow B represents a non-contact force.

questions.question: A book is resting on a wooden table. Which of the following is the most precise and standard way to label the upward force arrow acting on the book?
options: 'The upward force of the table'
'Force acting on the table by the book'
'Force acting on the book by the table'
'Gravity pulling down'

questions.question: A massive container ship and a small motorboat are both traveling at the same speed of 10 knots. Why does the container ship require a much larger braking force and distance to come to a complete stop?
options: Objects with a greater mass need a greater force to change their motion.
Small boats have more friction acting on them from the water.
Container ships experience less drag because of their streamlined shape.
The motorboat has a larger chemical energy store than the container ship.

questions.question: A lump of clay is sitting stationary on a workbench. A student presses down on it with their hand, flattening it. What role did the force from the hand play in this scenario?
options: The force was needed to change the shape of the clay.
The force was only needed to keep the clay stationary.
The force was not necessary because clay changes shape naturally over time.
The force was a non-contact force that didn't touch the clay.

questions.question: A toy boat experiences a forward thrust of 12 N from its propeller, a water resistance force of 8 N acting in the opposite direction, and a strong wind pushing it forward with a force of 3 N. What is the resultant force acting on the boat?
options: 17 N forward
7 N forward
23 N forward
1 N backward

questions.question: During a tug-of-war, Team A pulls to the left with a force of 450 N, while Team B pulls to the right with a force of 480 N. Which of the following describes the resulting motion and direction of the rope's center?
options: The rope moves to the left because the resultant force acts to the left.
The rope moves to the right because the resultant force acts to the right.
The rope does not move because both teams are pulling.
The rope moves to the right with a force of 930 N.

questions.question: Four identical shopping carts are pushed from rest. Cart A has a resultant force of 5 N, Cart B has 12 N, Cart C has 3 N, and Cart D has 8 N. Assuming all other factors are identical, which cart will experience the fastest change in speed?
options: Cart A
Cart B
Cart C
Cart D

questions.question: When we say a fully charged battery or a raised weight has energy, what does this fundamentally mean about the object in terms of physical interactions?
options: It contains a physical fluid called energy that flows out during a collision.
It possesses properties that allow it to interact with other objects, cause changes, or make things happen.
It is immune to external forces like friction and gravity until the energy is gone.
It must be actively moving or emitting light at that exact moment.

questions.question: Two highly polished metal blocks are placed together. Even though they look perfectly smooth to the naked eye, a microscopic analysis explains why a small frictional force still exists between them. Why does this friction occur?
options: The microscopic peaks and troughs on the surfaces still touch and lock together.
The blocks are chemically bonding and melting into a single piece.
The air pressure between the blocks is pushing them apart.
One block is always heavier than the other block.

questions.question: Before starting an experiment to measure the pulling force on a wooden block, a student notices that the pointer on their spring balance (newton meter) sits at 0.5 N when nothing is hanging from it. What action should the student take to ensure their measurements are accurate?
options: Subtract 0.5 N from only the final average of their results.
Adjust the scale or pointer to read zero when no force is applied.
Add 0.5 N to every reading they record during the experiment.
Proceed with the experiment since a small starting offset does not affect the force readings.

questions.question: A student needs to measure a small friction force expected to be around 0.8 N. They have three newton meters available: Meter X (range 0-1 N, divisions of 0.05 N), Meter Y (range 0-10 N, divisions of 0.5 N), and Meter Z (range 0-50 N, divisions of 5 N). Which meter should they select and why?
options: Meter Z, because its large range prevents it from breaking if the force is slightly higher.
Meter Y, because a 10 N scale is the standard size for all school laboratory experiments.
Meter X, because its scale is best suited to measure small forces with high precision.
Any of the meters, as they will all give the exact same reading of 0.8 N.

questions.question: An investigator tests how different materials (rubber, wood, steel, and plastic) affect the friction force when dragged across a concrete floor. How should they present their final data, and why?
options: A line graph, because the independent variable is continuous.
A bar chart, because the independent variable is categoric.
A scatter graph, because there are two continuous variables.
A pie chart, because the friction forces must add up to 100 percent.

questions.question: A mechanical engineer tests four different oils on a steel hinge to find the most effective lubricant. She measures the force needed to move the hinge before and after applying each oil. Which of the following results indicates the most effective lubricant?
options: Oil A: the force required to move the hinge increased by 2 N.
Oil B: the force required to move the hinge remained exactly the same.
Oil C: the force required to move the hinge decreased by 8 N.
Oil D: the force required to move the hinge decreased by 2 N.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a complete and scientifically sound conclusion for an investigation into how surface roughness affects friction?
options: We dragged a block over sandpaper, wood, and plastic, and we used a newton meter to record the forces.
The rougher the surface, the greater the friction force, because the sandpaper required a force of 4.5 N while the smooth plastic only required 1.2 N.
Friction is a contact force that slows things down, which is why cars have brakes made of rubber.
The experiment was a fair test because we used the same block and pulled it at the same speed every time.

questions.question: A group of students is investigating how the mass of a toy car affects the distance it travels after rolling down a ramp. To make this a fair test, which set of variables must they keep constant?
options: The mass of the car, the height of the ramp, and the release method.
The height of the ramp, the surface of the ramp, and the release method.
The mass of the car, the surface of the ramp, and the distance travelled.
The distance travelled, the time taken, and the mass of the car.

questions.question: A student holds a strong magnet near an iron paperclip resting on a table. Before the magnet even touches the paperclip, the paperclip leaps upward onto the magnet. Which statement correctly explains this observation?
options: Magnetic forces can only act when two objects are in direct physical contact.
Magnetic forces are non-contact forces that can act with or without physical contact.
The paperclip jumped because of air currents created by the movement of the hand.
Gravity stopped acting on the paperclip once the magnet was brought close.

questions.question: A skydiver falls through the air before opening their parachute. What is the nature of the drag force acting on the skydiver?
options: It is a non-contact force that pulls the skydiver toward the clouds.
It is a contact force caused by air particles pushing against the moving skydiver.
It is an electrostatic force that attracts the skydiver to the surrounding air.
It is a magnetic force that slows down the metal parts of the parachute.

questions.question: A student draws a force diagram of a swimmer. The arrow pointing forward (thrust) is drawn 4 cm long, while the arrow pointing backward (drag) is drawn 2 cm long. What does this difference in arrow length represent?
options: The thrust force is acting over a longer distance than the drag force.
The thrust force is twice as large in size as the drag force.
The swimmer is accelerating downwards because of the drag force.
The drag force is being applied for a longer period of time than the thrust.

questions.question: When drawing a force arrow to represent the upward normal contact force of the ground acting on a heavy box, where should the tail (starting point) of the arrow be positioned?
options: At the very top of the box, pointing towards the sky.
At the center of gravity of the Earth, pointing downwards.
At the point of contact between the bottom of the box and the ground.
Floating 2 cm above the box to avoid overlapping the diagram.

questions.question: A book rests on a wooden table. Which of the following is the most scientifically precise and complete label for the upward force supporting the book?
options: Upward force of gravity
Force acting on the table by the book
Force acting on the book by the table
Friction on the floor

questions.question: A massive cargo ship and a small speedboat are both travelling at 5 m/s. Why does the cargo ship require a much larger force and a longer distance to come to a complete stop compared to the speedboat?
options: The cargo ship has a smaller surface area in contact with the water.
The cargo ship has a greater mass, meaning it needs a greater force to change its motion.
The speedboat is affected by a larger gravity force due to its design.
Water resistance does not act on objects with a large mass.

questions.question: A lump of clay is sitting stationary on a workbench. Which of the following actions demonstrates that a force is required to change either its motion or its shape?
options: Leaving the clay untouched overnight so that it dries out.
Squeezing the clay with your hands to flatten it into a pancake.
Observing the clay while it remains perfectly still in a draft-free room.
Shifting your viewpoint to look at the clay from a different angle.

questions.question: An airplane travels at a constant speed of 250 m/s in a straight line. What can be concluded about the forces acting on the airplane?
options: The forward thrust must be much greater than the drag force to maintain this high speed.
The forces are balanced, meaning there is no resultant force and no change in speed.
There are no forces at all acting on the airplane while it is high in the air.
The lift force is the only active force keeping the airplane at a constant altitude.

questions.question: When a cyclist applies the brakes to slow down a bicycle, how is energy transferred between the system's stores by the action of forces?
options: Energy is destroyed by the friction force, reducing the total energy in the universe.
Mechanical work done by the friction force transfers energy from the kinetic store to the thermal store of the brakes.
The kinetic energy is converted into a physical force that vanishes once the bicycle stops.
Chemical energy is transferred directly into gravitational energy without any force acting.
